title: TwoSpeedStrategist sends event-driven and replan requests to the fast (Refine) strategist when the event arrived while a request was in flight
description: TwoSpeedStrategist decides that a request is event-driven with `context.Features.Events.Any(e => e.Time > previous)`. FeatureCompiler emits each StrategicEvent in exactly one compile, so `Features.Events` only holds events from the current frame. StrategyScheduler defers a trigger that arrives while the primary is in flight (`pendingTrigger`) and starts that request later, on a frame whose Events are usually empty. The deferred event request therefore goes to the fast strategist. Replan triggers (`replan:abort`, `replan:base_threat`, `replan:trigger`) are not events, so they never reach the slow strategist either. The Refine strategist is documented as not allowed to answer a changed situation and fails with `claude.refine_playbook_switch` if it tries to switch playbook. In addition, `lastSlow` was already stamped for the slow request that the same event late-discarded, so no slow answer comes for up to 20 s. In the llm+fast arm (cadence 5 s, fake latency 4 s) the primary is in flight about 80% of the time, so most major events are misrouted.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary test, now deleted. Setup: Scheduler(primary = TwoSpeed(slow, fast, 20), cadence 5). t=0: an initial request goes to slow. t=2: a BaseUnderAttack event (severity 0.9) arrives while slow is in flight. t=3: slow completes. Result: the slow answer is late-discarded (late=1). The request that the event triggered (trigger `event:BaseUnderAttack`) starts at t=3 and goes to fast (slowCalls=1, fastCalls=1). The bot cannot change playbook in answer to the attack until the next 20 s slow slot.
suggested_fix: Pass the trigger reason (or a `SituationChanged` flag) in StrategistContext and route every `event:*` and `replan:*` trigger to slow. Otherwise TwoSpeed has to track events itself across frames through IFrameAwareStrategist instead of reading only the current frame's Events. Stamp `lastSlow` only when the slow result was applied, or reset it when that result is discarded or fails.

title: Decision-log content, and the LLM prompt, depend on the process culture, so hashes differ between machines and locales
description: DecisionLogCodec's contract says equal logs hash equal on every machine and locale, but strings that end up in the log use culture-sensitive interpolation of doubles. Examples: the bandit rationale $"LinUCB: mean {bestMean:0.000}, width {bestWidth:0.000}" (and the defend rationale at line 59), which is logged inside the Proposal and IntentActivated intent JSON. The ArmyValueSwing event detail $"{fraction:P0} in 15s" and LowPower $"deficit {deficit:0}" (FeatureCompiler.Events.cs:104,120) go into the Claude prompt, which changes the logged inputTokens. Others are the validator messages in IntentValidator.cs (for example lines 56, 94, 153 and 235, written into validation records), the DistilledStrategist rationales, and the OperationalPlanner notes. Nothing sets InvariantGlobalization or the invariant culture.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with the same bandit match (rush, twin-valley, seed 1) run under two cultures. With CultureInfo.CurrentCulture=en-US the hash is 89d1c7b7...; with fi-FI it is 8ed8f217..., and line 1 differs: "rationale":"LinUCB: mean 0.000, width 4.797" against "LinUCB: mean 0,000, width 4,797". For the llm arm (--llm-fake) the hash is 73838ecd... against 42361954..., and line 556 differs in cost.inputTokens (4028 against 4029) because the prompt text changed. A log recorded on one machine therefore fails hash comparison when replayed or re-run on a machine with another locale, and a live Claude model receives locale-formatted numbers.
suggested_fix: Set <InvariantGlobalization>true</InvariantGlobalization> for the bot, sim, Claude and arena projects in Directory.Build.props, and/or format every such string with string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...). Enable CA1305 as an error under TreatWarningsAsErrors so new cases fail the build.

title: Arena datasets carry no observation mode, so oracle-run decisions can silently train a Belief-mode distilled arm
description: An `--oracle` arena run writes dataset-<arm>-oracle.ndjson from decisions made on oracle features (full enemy army, all regions visible). DecisionExample has no observation-mode field, FromDecisionLog does not read features.Mode, and ReadNdjson accepts every line. `--dataset` in a normal (Belief) run therefore loads oracle-derived examples without complaint. The distilled arm then plays in Belief mode with a policy fitted to omniscient features. Its results are reported as a Belief arm; the only hint is the free-text label `distilled-from:<filename>`.
failure_scenario: Run `arena run --oracle --arms selector --out o`, which writes o/dataset-selector-oracle.ndjson. Then run `arena run --arms distilled --dataset o/dataset-selector-oracle.ndjson`. The distilled arm's classifier is trained on vectors where enemy army value and coverage came from oracle frames. It is evaluated and reported as a fog-respecting arm, with no oracle label and no rejection.
suggested_fix: Record the observation mode (from StrategicFeatures.Mode or the arm spec) in each DecisionExample and in the IntentActivated payload. Make FromDecisionLog and ReadNdjson reject Oracle-mode examples, or have the arena refuse them, unless the consuming run is itself an oracle run. When one is accepted, add an `oracle` label to the distilled arm.

title: TwoSpeedStrategist sends a fallback or emergency placeholder to the fast Refine model; its renewal promotes the placeholder to a primary commitment and the LLM's next choice is refused
description: `slowDue` looks only at `context.ActiveIntent is null`, the time of the last slow request, and new events. It records `lastSlow` when a slow request starts, not when the slow model's choice is applied. If a slow request fails (refusal, parse failure, rate limit, late discard), the active intent is the fallback selector's placeholder, and every 5 s cadence request for up to 20 s goes to the fast Refine model. Refine keeps the active playbook and posture, so the arbiter treats the answer as a 'renewal', and Renew() sets ActiveRole = Primary ('A primary strategist endorsing a placeholder's plan makes it a real commitment'). ActiveSince keeps the fallback's activation time. When the slow LLM next proposes a different playbook, the placeholder is no longer yieldable, and the proposal is refused by commitment or hysteresis. Without this, it would have replaced the fallback at once ('yield'). The renewal also re-stamps the intent's Source as Llm (in the real Refined(), Source = IntentSource.Llm), so the selector's choice is logged and counted as the LLM's.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a scratch xUnit test (real StrategyScheduler, IntentArbiter, IntentValidator and TwoSpeedStrategist, cadence 5 s). At t=0 the slow request is sent and the fallback installs fb-0 (generic-defend, Fallback). At t=1 the slow call returns null. At t=5, 10 and 15 the fast Refine renews fb-0 as role Primary ('renewal'). At t=20 slow is asked again, and at t=22 it answers allied-boom Boom with confidence 0.9. Result: arbitrationReason 'commitment', refused. Active stays refine-225 (generic-defend). Control run, same scenario with the slow strategist alone: the LLM choice is activated at t=22 ('yield').
suggested_fix: In TwoSpeedStrategist, route to the slow strategist whenever the active intent was not installed by the slow strategist (placeholder or fallback source, or an ActiveIntent that is not the last slow-accepted intent), and do not count a slow request as served until it produced an applied intent. Alternatively, have the arbiter keep ActiveRole as the placeholder role when the renewal comes from a refinement of a placeholder.

- **Refine output:** src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot.Claude/ClaudeStrategist.cs:276-288. `Refined(active, proposed) => active with { ..., Source = IntentSource.Llm, ... }` keeps the playbook and posture.

title: The bandit credits every proposal with the match reward, including the ones the arbiter refused and that never took effect
description: ProposeAsync records `(x, best.Id)` into `episode` when it proposes, and the arena's CompleteEpisode(reward) applies the match reward to every recorded entry. A proposal is only a request: the scheduler can late-discard it, the validator can reject it, and the arbiter can refuse it (abort_firing, commitment, hysteresis). No arbitration outcome is ever fed back, so LinUCB updates playbooks that were never played with the result of a match played by a different intent, often the fallback's. This corrupts the bandit's estimates, and with them the bandit arm's win rate as a learning result.
failure_scenario: Arena run on a git-archive copy of HEAD (`run --arms bandit --opponents balanced,rush --seeds 2 --maps training`), with temporary instrumentation that counts the primary arbitration reasons per bandit match. In one match the bandit made 88 proposals, 54 of them refused 'abort_firing'. Other matches had 13, 6, 3, 2 and 2 refusals from 'commitment' or 'hysteresis'. In total, 80 bandit proposals over 12 matches never took effect, yet each one went into `episode` and was credited with the match reward by CompleteEpisode.
suggested_fix: Record episode entries only for decisions that became or stayed active. For example, let the harness feed arbitration outcomes back (IOutcomeLearner.Observe on strategy.intent_activated records for the bandit's own intent ids). Or have CompleteEpisode take the list of applied intent ids and drop the other pending entries.
